accepted.question_text: Which term-rewriting systems can be directly represented inside lambda calculus, in the sense that lambda terms represent the rewrite-system operators and each rewrite step in the system translates to a lambda-calculus reduction? Are there universal rewrite systems for this notion of direct definability?

evidence.quote: Which rewrite systems can be directly defined in lambda calculus?

accepted.question_text: For a term-rewriting system R and a term t, define Spec(t) as the complete partial order of finite and infinite reduction sequences starting at t, modulo the quasi-order under which one sequence is below another when every term in the first eventually reduces to some term in the second. What properties does this spectrum have for special classes of rewrite systems, especially orthogonal systems and non-erasing systems, and how do those properties change when spectra of orthogonal systems are quotiented by Levy-style permutation equivalence?

evidence.quote: Investigate the properties of spectri for special classes of rewrite systems.

accepted.question_text: What is the computational complexity of deciding ground reducibility for a finite term-rewriting system R and a term t, where t is ground reducible when every ground, variable-free instance of t contains a redex; in particular, can the known general and left-linear upper and lower bounds be improved?

evidence.quote: What is the complexity of deciding ground-reducibility?

accepted.question_text: Given a term in ordinary untyped lambda calculus, is it decidable whether that term can be assigned a type in the second-order lambda-2 calculus?

evidence.quote: Given a term in ordinary untyped lambda calculus, is it decidable whether it can be typed in the second-order λ2 calculus?

accepted.question_text: Do the surjective pairing axioms D1(D x y) = x, D2(D x y) = y, and D(D1 x)(D2 x) = x conservatively extend lambda-beta-eta conversion on pure untyped lambda terms? More generally, is surjective pairing conservative over every lambda theory or extension of Combinatory Logic, or are there theories for which conservative extension by surjective pairing fails?

evidence.quote: Does surjective pairing conservatively extend λβη-conversion?

accepted.question_text: Let R and S be left-linear term-rewriting systems over disjoint vocabularies. If each system has unicity of normal forms with respect to reduction, meaning any two normal forms reachable by reduction from the same term are identical, must the union R union S also have unicity of normal forms with respect to reduction?

evidence.quote: Is unicity of normal forms with respect to reduction a modular property of left-linear term-rewriting systems?

accepted.question_text: Given a finite term-rewriting system, is it decidable whether the set of its ground normal forms is a regular tree language?

evidence.quote: Is it possible to decide whether the set of ground normal forms with respect to a given (finite) term-rewriting system is a regular tree language?

accepted.question_text: For orthogonal term-rewriting systems, is the decision problem for strong sequentiality NP-complete?

evidence.quote: Is the decidability of strong sequentiality for orthogonal term rewriting systems NP-complete?

accepted.question_text: Thatte showed that an orthogonal constructor-based rewrite system is left-sequential exactly when it is strongly sequential. Does this equivalence extend to all orthogonal term-rewriting systems? If not, is left-sequentiality decidable for orthogonal systems?

evidence.quote: Is left-sequentiality a decidable property of orthogonal systems?

accepted.question_text: Let a term-rewriting system, or more generally a system with bound variables, be finitely generated, full in the sense that its terms are all terms generated from its function symbols, and Church-Rosser. Must it have a recursive one-step reduction strategy that always reaches a normal form when one exists?

evidence.quote: Has any full, finitely-generated and Church-Rosser term-rewriting system (or system with bound variables) a recursive, one-step, normalizing reduction strategy?

accepted.question_text: For standard, join-style conditional term-rewriting systems whose rules have the form p implies l rewrites to r and whose conditions require terms to be joinable, is unicity of normal forms a modular property?

evidence.quote: Is unicity of normal forms a modular property of standard conditional systems?

accepted.question_text: For ground, variable-free term-rewriting systems, what is the complexity of deciding confluence?

evidence.quote: What is the complexity of the decision problem for the confluence of ground term-rewriting systems?

accepted.question_text: For left-linear term-rewriting systems, can one give decidable criteria that guarantee the Church-Rosser property, such as criteria based on whether each critical pair t approximately s satisfies s reducing to t in one parallel step, s reducing to t by zero or one steps, or one side reducing to the other by zero or one steps?

evidence.quote: Give decidable criteria for left-linear rewriting systems to be Church-Rosser.

accepted.question_text: For conditional rewrite systems, under what syntactic restrictions does parallel rewriting enjoy subcommutativity, a strong form of confluence analogous to the subcommutativity of parallel rewriting in orthogonal term-rewriting systems?

evidence.quote: Which conditional rewrite systems are subcommutative?

accepted.question_text: Consider Combinatory Logic extended with Boolean constants T and F and a conditional constant C, with rules I x -> x, K x y -> x, S x y z -> (x z)(y z), C T x y -> x, C F x y -> y, and the semi-equational rule that x is convertible to y implies C z x y -> x. Is this nonterminating semi-equational conditional rewrite system confluent?

evidence.quote: Is the extension of Combinatory Logic by Boolean constants confluent?

accepted.question_text: Let R be a normal conditional term-rewriting system with conditions s ->! t, where t is a ground normal form of s, and let Rse be the corresponding semi-equational conditional rewrite system with conditions s convertible to t. Under what conditions does confluence of Rse imply confluence of R?
accepted.context_brief: Confluence transfer for normal conditional systems

evidence.quote: Under what conditions does confluence of a normal semi-equational conditional term rewriting system imply confluence of the associated oriented system?

accepted.question_text: For the semi-equational conditional term-rewriting system that linearizes Combinatory Logic extended with surjective pairing, with rules I x -> x, K x y -> x, S x y z -> (x z)(y z), D1(D x y) -> x, D2(D x y) -> y, and conditional rules from convertibility to D(D1 x)(D2 y) -> x and D(D1 x)(D2 y) -> y, is the system confluent? If it is confluent, does it have an effective normal-form strategy?

evidence.quote: Is a certain conditional rewrite system, which is a linearization of Combinatory Logic extended with surjective pairing, confluent?

accepted.question_text: In infinitary rewriting for orthogonal term-rewriting systems, does the almost-confluence result known for strongly convergent infinite reduction sequences remain valid when infinite reduction sequences are interpreted using the more liberal Cauchy-convergence notion?

evidence.quote: Does “almost-confluence” hold for convergent infinite reduction sequences?

accepted.question_text: Can strong normalization of typed lambda calculus be proved by a reasonably straightforward mapping from typed terms to a well-founded ordering, even though beta-reduction can leave the type structure unchanged? Does the same approach work for polymorphic, second-order lambda calculus?

evidence.quote: Can strong normalization of the typed lambda calculus be proved by a reasonably straightforward mapping from typed terms to a well-founded ordering?

accepted.question_text: For a one-rule length-preserving string-rewriting, or semi-Thue, system, what is the best upper bound on the length of a derivation as a function of the length n of the initial string and the size k of the rule?
accepted.context_brief: Derivation length for one-rule string rewriting

evidence.quote: What is the best bound on the length of a derivation for a one-rule length-preserving string-rewriting system?

accepted.question_text: Is termination decidable for a single rewrite rule that is both left-linear and right-linear? Relatedly, what is known about decidability of termination or confluence for one monadic or non-monadic string rewrite rule?

evidence.quote: Is termination of one linear rule decidable?

accepted.question_text: Can practical methods be devised for proving termination of standard conditional rewriting systems, despite the interdependence between normalization and termination in such systems?

evidence.quote: Devise practical methods for proving termination of conditional rewriting systems.

accepted.question_text: For the rewrite system encoding the Battle of Hydra and Hercules, which is terminating but not provably terminating in Peano Arithmetic, must every termination ordering that proves its termination have the Howard ordinal as its order type?

evidence.quote: Must any termination ordering used for proving termination of the Battle of Hydra and Hercules-system have the Howard ordinal as its order type?

accepted.question_text: For recursive path ordering with multiset and lexicographic status, is the existential fragment of the first-order theory of ordering constraints decidable when the precedence on function symbols is partial rather than total?

evidence.quote: Is satisfiability of lpo or rpo ordering constraints decidable in case of non-total precedences?

accepted.question_text: For a finite function-symbol set containing at least one associative-commutative function symbol, let T be the set of ground terms modulo the AC axioms. Is the Sigma-2 fragment of the first-order theory of T decidable, especially the complement problem asking whether a term has an instance not matching any of a finite family of other terms modulo AC?

evidence.quote: Is the Σ2-fragment of the first-order theory of ground terms modulo AC decidable?

accepted.question_text: For a non-orthogonal term-rewriting or combinatory reduction system R, suppose redexes can be mapped to a well-founded linear order so that residual redex degrees never increase and newly created redexes have strictly smaller degree than their creator. Does this decreasing-redexes property imply termination? If not, which useful subclasses still satisfy the implication?

evidence.quote: Is it true for non-orthogonal systems that decreasing redexes implies termination?

accepted.question_text: How can Lescanne's notion of well-rewrite-ordering, an extension of term embedding and simplification ordering, be extended to form the basis of a new kind of recursive path ordering?

evidence.quote: How can the notion of well-rewrite-ordering be used to as the basis for some new kind of “recursive path ordering”?

accepted.question_text: Can effective and implementable methods be developed to decide whether a rewrite system decreases with respect to some exponential interpretation, analogous to existing methods for polynomial interpretations?

evidence.quote: Develop effective methods to decide whether a system decreases with respect to some exponential interpretation.

accepted.question_text: Which is the coarsest relation such that, for every terminating rewrite relation, the union of that relation with the coarser relation preserves termination and remains fully invariant under instantiation? Without full invariance, is encompassment the coarsest relation that preserves termination?

evidence.quote: Which is the coarsest relation such that its union with any rewrite relation preserves termination?

accepted.question_text: What are the computational complexities of term-ordering decision problems, including comparability under recursive path ordering with a suitable precedence and lexicographic path ordering with non-total precedences or variables?

evidence.quote: What are the complexities of various term ordering decision problems?

accepted.question_text: Is there a decidable uniform word problem for which no variant of rewriting, such as rewriting modulo a congruence with decidable matching or ordered rewriting, can decide the problem without adding new symbols to the vocabulary?
accepted.context_brief: Limits of rewriting for word problems

evidence.quote: Is there a decidable uniform word problem for which there is no variant on the rewriting theme that can decide it—without adding new symbols?

accepted.question_text: Is there any finite term-rewriting system, of an appropriate kind, for free lattices?

evidence.quote: Is there a finite term-rewriting system of some kind for free lattices?

accepted.question_text: How can completion modulo associativity, commutativity, identity, and idempotence be handled effectively, given that techniques for AC-completion and ACU-completion do not directly carry over to idempotence?

evidence.quote: How can completion modulo ACUI be made effective?

accepted.question_text: For an equational theory E and an ordering greater-than, is there a set of inference rules that always succeeds in computing a convergent set of rewrite rules R whenever such an R exists for the ordering, even when the ordering cannot be made total on ground terms?

evidence.quote: Is there a set of inference rules that always succeeds in computing a convergent set of rewrite rules for a given set of equations and an ordering, provided that it exists?

accepted.question_text: If a completion procedure is allowed to change the ordering during the run, using at each step an ordering that orients the current rules but not necessarily deleted old rules, can the procedure become incomplete, leaving persisting rules that are not confluent?

evidence.quote: Can completion be incomplete when the ordering is changed en route?

accepted.question_text: For Boolean-ring based methods for resolution-like first-order theorem proving, can more restrictive strategies be found, such as strategies using only single overlaps or only unifications of maximal atoms, while preserving completeness?

evidence.quote: Find more restrictive strategies in Boolean-ring based methods for resolution-like first-order theorem proving.

accepted.question_text: For contextual deduction, a rewriting-like clausal reasoning mechanism that uses pattern matching rather than unification and instantiates clauses only to match existing clauses, is there a useful notion of complete theory under which contextual deduction is complete for refuting ground clauses?

evidence.quote: Is there a notion of “complete theory” for which contextual deduction is complete for refutation of ground clauses?

accepted.question_text: Is unification modulo the theory of distributivity, with one right-distributivity axiom and one left-distributivity axiom, decidable?

evidence.quote: Is unification modulo distributivity decidable?

accepted.question_text: In rules for computing dag-solved forms of unification problems in equational theories, can the Merge rule condition requiring s to be a non-variable no larger than t be replaced by the condition that Check* does not apply; equivalently, is Check* complete for finding cycles under this modified Merge rule?

evidence.quote: Can the application condition on the Merge rule in the computation of dag-solved forms of unification problems be improved?

accepted.question_text: For associative-commutative unification, do the same or similar transformation rules known to terminate with variable replacement after every step or at the end also terminate under more flexible control strategies?

evidence.quote: Does AC unification terminate under more flexible control?

accepted.question_text: What is the complexity of the first-order theory of finite trees over finitely many symbols, and is that theory in PSPACE? What is the corresponding complexity for infinite trees?

evidence.quote: What is the complexity of the first-order theory of trees?

accepted.question_text: For first-order formulas over trees with equality as the only predicate, can negation be effectively eliminated from any formula that is equivalent to a positive formula; equivalently, when such a formula has a finite complete set of unifiers, can that set be computed?

evidence.quote: Can negations be effectivly eliminated from first-order formulas over trees, where equality is the only predicate?

accepted.question_text: Can one design a general framework for combining constraint-solving algorithms, including algorithms for unification, equations and disequations, shared constants or constructors, membership constraints, and non-free solution domains?

evidence.quote: Design a framework for combining constraint solving algorithms.

accepted.question_text: For every finitary unification problem in a syntactic equational theory, can pruning or freezing rules be designed so that the derivation tree generated by syntactic unification rules becomes finite and yields a finite complete set of unifiers?

evidence.quote: How to compute finite and complete sets of unifiers for any finitary unification problem of a syntactic equational theory.

Springer and Tel Aviv metadata confirmed the same title and authors; Springer exposed only metadata and the exact CWI PDF could not be downloaded locally because DNS/network access was unavailable. The readable RTA-list text was used only for the April 1991 problem statements that correspond to the original RTA 1991 list; later December 1991 and subsequent additions were excluded.

Extracted forty-four April 1991 problem blocks, preserving solved markers when headings or remarks explicitly resolved an item.
Rewrote each extracted summary into a standalone question by inlining the definitions and rule schemata visible in the same problem block where needed.
No near-duplicate problem statements were merged; the numbered RTA problems are distinct.
